name: Pediatric SNT Integration: The Ethics of Augmenting Children
author: GLMZ Pediatric Ethics Board
body:
Children's nervous systems are still developing. SNT neural bridging in a developing brain is not the same process as in an adult brain. The implications are profound and deeply contested.

When SNT is applied to a child under 12, the neural bridges do not merely connect to existing pathways — they become part of the developmental architecture. The child's brain grows around the implant. The implant becomes as native as a biological organ. Integration rates in pediatric patients are 99.8% — higher than adults — because the developing brain adapts to include the hardware in its fundamental wiring.

This means a child who receives a cybernetic implant with SNT bonding will integrate it more deeply than any adult patient ever could. The implant will feel more natural, respond more fluidly, and become more intrinsically linked to the child's sense of self.

It also means that removing the implant later — for any reason — is catastrophically more traumatic than adult explantation. The brain did not adapt to the implant. The brain grew to include it. Removal is not losing a tool. It is losing a developmental structure.

CURRENT GUIDELINES:
— Medical necessity implants (cochlear, cardiac, respiratory) are permitted at any age with parental consent
— Elective augmentation is prohibited under age 16 in most GLMZ jurisdictions
— No jurisdiction prohibits parental consent for augmentation of children over 12
— Three corponations (Tessera, Axiom, Slagworks) offer 'Legacy Programs' that provide free augmentation to employees' children as young as 8, with the contractual requirement that the child work for the corponation upon reaching employment age

The Legacy Programs are, in the Board's assessment, indentured servitude secured by neurological dependency. A child augmented at 8 with corponation-specific hardware bonded by SNT cannot leave the corponation at 18 without losing implants that their brain grew around. The corponation owns the hardware. The SNT made the hardware part of the child. The child is, in every meaningful sense, owned.

This Board recommends prohibiting elective augmentation below age 16 across all GLMZ jurisdictions. This recommendation has been made annually for seven years. It has been adopted by zero corponations.
